history.sg_progress: The Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs is looking into different business models to address the issue of any conflicting roles. Some of the models for the feasibility study are: (a) having the low-value acquisitions centralized in one person; (b) conducting analysis on the procurement roles and transferring some of those roles from one person to other colleagues in the region; (c) discussing with the Procurement Division the best model for the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs given the nature of its mandate and the agility required in crisis response; (d) removing the travel roles in some instances to avoid the conflicts through the review of the footprint in the specific region.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration conduct a comprehensive review of roles assigned in Umoja in conjunction with the delegation of authority and identify and address the issue of conflicting roles.
history.administration_response: Following a comprehensive review of roles assigned in Umoja, the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs has resolved all conflicting roles regarding the segregation of duties except one. The Office had intended to hire a female staff member to assume the duties of one user left who still had a conflicting role. However, owing to the country authorities’ de facto ban on hiring Afghan female nationals, the user deprovisioning could not be completed. The Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs will resume the recruitment of Afghan female nationals as soon as the country’s regulatory regime allows. In the meantime, the Office is also considering other alternative solutions, and requests the closure of this recommendation by the Board.
history.board_assessment: Given that all conflicting roles regarding the segregation of duties have been resolved, the Board considers this recommendation implemented.
